notes.claim: Newton's law of cooling gives the rate of cooling of a liquid as proportional to the difference between its temperature and its surroundings' temperature.
The slope of the solution curve through a point is set by the equation itself, as y′ = f(x, y) at that point.

sources.title: 19 19 — Loughborough University (HELM)
sources.quote: Newton’s law of cooling states that the rate of cooling of liquid is proportional to the difference between its temperature and the temperature of its environment (the ambient temperature).

sources.title: ES.1803 S24: Reading: Topic 11: Numerical Methods for First-Order Differential Equations — MIT OpenCourseWare
sources.quote: We know that the slope of the solution curve through (𝑥0, 𝑦0) is 𝑦 ′ = 𝑓(𝑥0, 𝑦0).
